text: When a missile is fired from a ship, the probability that it is intercepted is $\frac{1}{3}$ and the probability that the missile hits the target, given that it is not intercepted, is $\frac{3}{4}$. If three missiles are fired independently from the ship, then the probability that all three hit the target, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Probability of not getting intercepted = $\frac{2}{3}$

When it is not intercepted, probability of missile hitting target = $\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore$ So when such 3 missiles launched
then P (all 3 hitting the target) 

= $\left (\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{3}{4}\right )$ $\times$ $\left (\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{3}{4}\right )$ $\times$ $\left (\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{3}{4}\right )$  

$=\frac{1}{8}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: The value of $\int\limits _{-1}^{1}x^{2}e^{[x^{3}]}dx$, where [ t ] denotes the greatest integer $\leq$ t, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int\limits _{-1}^{1}x^{2}e^{[x^{3}]}dx$

Here -1 $\leq$ x $\leq$ 1 then -1 $\leq$ $x^{3}$ $\leq$ 1

Integer between -1 and 1 is 0. So integration will be divided into two parts, -1 to 0 and 0 to 1.

$=\int\limits _{-1}^{0}x^{2}e^{[x^{3}]}dx+\int\limits _{0}^{1}x^{2}e^{[x^{3}]}dx$

$=\int\limits _{-1}^{0}x^{2}e^{-1}dx+\int\limits _{0}^{1}x^{2}e^{0}dx$

= $\frac{1}{e}\times \left [\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right ]_{-1}^{0}+\left [\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right ]_{0}^{1}$

$=\frac{1}{e}\times \left (0-\left (\frac{-1}{3}\right )\right )+\frac{1}{3}$

$=\frac{1}{3e}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{1+e}{3e}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: The total number of positive integral solutions (x, y, z) such that xyz = 24 is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$24=2^{3}\times 3$, so each of $x,y,z$ is of the form $2^{a}\quad 3^{b}$, where the exponents of 2 add up to 3 and the exponents of 3 add up to 1.

The three factors 2 are shared among $x,y,z$ (each may receive 0, 1, 2 or 3 of them) in ${}^{3+3-1}C_{3-1}={}^{5}C_{2}=10$ ways.

The single factor 3 goes to one of $x,y,z$ in 3 ways.

Number of ordered triples $=10\times 3=30$. These are the orderings of $\{1,1,24\}$ and $\{2,2,6\}$ (3 each) and of $\{1,2,12\}$, $\{1,3,8\}$, $\{1,4,6\}$, $\{2,3,4\}$ (6 each): $6+24=30$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: If a curve passes through the origin and the slope of the tangent to it at any point (x, y) is $\frac{x^{2}-4x+y+8}{x-2}$, then this curve also passes through the point :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given

y (0) = 0

& $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{(x-2)^{2}+y+4}{x-2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{y}{x-2}=(x-2)+\frac{4}{x-2}$

$\Rightarrow I.F.=e^{-\int \frac{1}{x-2}dx}=\frac{1}{x-2}$

Solution of D.E.

$\Rightarrow y.\frac{1}{x-2}=\int \frac{1}{x-2}\left ((x-2)+\frac{4}{x-2}\right ).dx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{y}{x-2}=x-\frac{4}{x-2}+C$

Now, at x = 0, y = 0 $\Rightarrow$ C = $-$2

$\therefore$ y = x (x $-$ 2) $-$ 4 $-$ 2 (x $-$ 2)

$\Rightarrow$ $y = x^{2}$ $-$ 4x

This curve passes through (5, 5)

text: Let the lines (2 $-$ i)z = (2 + i)$z–$ and (2 $+$ i)z + (i $-$ 2)$z–$ $-$ 4i = 0, (here $i^{2} =$ $-$1) be normal to a circle C. If the line iz + $z–$ + 1 + i = 0 is tangent to this circle C, then its radius is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(2-i)z=(2+i)z–$

$\Rightarrow (2-i)(x+iy)=(2+i)(x-iy)$

$\Rightarrow 2x-ix+2iy+y=2x+ix-2-iy+y$

$\Rightarrow 2ix-4iy=0$

$L_{1}:x-2y=0$

$\Rightarrow (2+i)z+(i-2)z–-4i=0$

$\Rightarrow (2+i)(x+iy)+(i-2)(x-iy)-4i=0$

$\Rightarrow 2x+ix+2iy-y+ix-2x+y+2iy-4i=0$

$\Rightarrow 2ix+4iy-4i=0$

$L_{2}:x+2y-2=0$

Solve $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}_{}$: x = 1, $4y=2,y=\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ $x=1$

Centre $\left (1,\frac{1}{2}\right )$

$L_{3}:iz+z–+1+i=0$

$\Rightarrow i(x+iy)+x-iy+1+i=0$

$\Rightarrow ix-y+x-iy+1+i=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-y+1)+i(x-y+1)=0$

Radius = distance from $\left (1,\frac{1}{2}\right )$ to $x-y+1=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $r=\frac{1-\frac{1}{2}+1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $r=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: Let $α$ be the angle between the lines whose direction cosines satisfy the equations l + m $-$ n = 0 and $l^{2} + m^{2}$ $-$ $n^{2} = 0$. Then the value of $\sin ^{4}α$ $+ \cos ^{4}α$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$l^{2}+m^{2}+n^{2}=1$

$\therefore$ $2n^{2}=1$ ($\because$ $l^{2} + m^{2}$ $-$ $n^{2} = 0)$

$\Rightarrow n=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\therefore$ $l^{2}+m^{2}=\frac{1}{2}$ & $l+m=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}-2lm=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow lm=0$ or $m=0$

$\therefore$ $l=0,m=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ or $l=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$<0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}>$ or $<\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}>$

$\therefore$ $\cos α=0+0+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ $\sin ^{4}α+\cos ^{4}α=1-\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{2}(2α)=1-\frac{1}{2}.\frac{3}{4}=\frac{5}{8}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

a, b, c $\in$ {1,2,3,4,5,6}

For equal roots, D = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $b^{2} = 4ac$

Favourable case :

$\therefore$ Required probability = $\frac{5}{216}$

text: The locus of the point of intersection of the lines $\left (\sqrt{3}\right )kx+ky-4\sqrt{3}=0$ and $\sqrt{3}x-y-4\left (\sqrt{3}\right )k=0$ is a conic, whose eccentricity is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $(x,y)$ be the point of intersection.

From the first line, $k\left (\sqrt{3}x+y\right )=4\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow \sqrt{3}x+y=\dfrac{4\sqrt{3}}{k}$.

From the second line, $\sqrt{3}x-y=4\sqrt{3}k$.

Multiplying the two eliminates $k$:

$3x^{2}-y^{2}=48\Rightarrow \dfrac{x^{2}}{16}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{48}=1$

This is a hyperbola with $a^{2}=16$ and $b^{2}=48$, so

$e^{2}=1+\dfrac{48}{16}=4\Rightarrow e=2$

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: The total number of numbers, lying between 100 and 1000 that can be formed with the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, if the repetition of digits is not allowed and numbers are divisible by either 3 or 5, is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The numbers are lying between 100 and 1000
then each number is of three digits.

The possible combination of 3 digits numbers
are

1, 2, 3; 1, 2, 4; 1, 2, 5; 1, 3, 4; 1, 3, 5; 1, 4, 5;
2, 3, 4; 2, 3, 5; 2, 4, 5; and 3, 4, 5.

The possible combination of numbers which are divisible by 3 are 1, 2,
3; 3, 4, 5; 1, 3, 5 and 2, 3, 4.

(If sum of digits of a number is divisible by 3 then the number is divisible by 3)

$\therefore$ Total number of numbers = 4 × 3! = 24

The possible combination of numbers divisible by 5 are 1, 2, 5; 2, 3, 5; 3, 4, 5; 1, 3, 5;
1, 4, 5 and 2, 4, 5.

(If the last digit of a number is 0 or 5 then the number is divisible by 5)

$\therefore$ Total number of numbers = 6 × 2! = 12

The possible combination of number divisible by both 3 and 5 are 1, 3, 5 and 3, 4, 5.

$\therefore$ Total number of numbers = 2 $\times$ 2! = 4

$\therefore$ Total required number = 24 + 12 - 4 = 32
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text:
If $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 0 & -\tan \left (\frac{θ}{2}\right ) \\ \tan \left (\frac{θ}{2}\right ) & 0 \end{array}\right ]$ and 
$(I_{2}+A)(I_{2}-A)^{-1}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & -b \\ b & a \end{array}\right ]$, then $13(a^{2}+b^{2})$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 0 & -\tan \frac{θ}{2} \\ \tan \frac{θ}{2} & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow I+A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -\tan \frac{θ}{2} \\ \tan \frac{θ}{2} & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow I-A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & \tan \frac{θ}{2} \\ -\tan \frac{θ}{2} & 1 \end{array}\right ]$ { $\therefore$ $|I-A|=\sec ^{2}θ/2$}

$\Rightarrow (I-A)^{-1}=\frac{1}{\sec ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -\tan \frac{θ}{2} \\ \tan \frac{θ}{2} & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow (I+A)(I-A)^{-1}$

$=\frac{1}{\sec ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -\tan \frac{θ}{2} \\ \tan \frac{θ}{2} & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -\tan \frac{θ}{2} \\ \tan \frac{θ}{2} & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$=\frac{1}{\sec ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1-\tan ^{2}\frac{θ}{2} & -2\tan \frac{θ}{2} \\ 2\tan \frac{θ}{2} & 1-\tan ^{2}\frac{θ}{2} \end{array}\right ]$

$a=\frac{1-\tan ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}}{\sec ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}}$

$b=\frac{2\tan \frac{θ}{2}}{\sec ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}}$

$\therefore$ $a^{2}+b^{2}=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $13(a^{2}+b^{2})$ = 13
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$, $\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}$ and $\vec{c}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$ be three given vectors. If $\vec{r}$ is a vector such that $\vec{r}\times \vec{a}=\vec{c}\times \vec{a}$ and $\vec{r}.\vec{b}=0$, then $\vec{r}.\vec{a}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$,

$\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}$,

$\vec{c}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$

$\vec{r}\times \vec{a}=\vec{c}\times \vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}\times \vec{a}-\vec{c}\times \vec{a}=0$

$\Rightarrow (\vec{r}-\vec{c})\times \vec{a}=0$

$\therefore$ $\vec{r}-\vec{c}=λ\vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}=λ\vec{a}+\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{b}=λ\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{c}.\vec{b}$ (taking dot with $\vec{b}$)

$\Rightarrow 0=λ\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{c}.\vec{b}$ [$\because$ $\vec{r}\quad .\vec{b}=0$]

$\Rightarrow λ(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}).(\hat{i}-\hat{j})+(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\widehat{k}).(\hat{i}-\hat{j})=0$

$\Rightarrow λ(1-2)+2=0$

$\Rightarrow λ=2$

$\therefore$ $\vec{r}=2\vec{a}+\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{a}=2\vec{a}.\vec{a}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}$ [taking dot with $\vec{a}$]

$=2\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}+\vec{a}.\vec{c}$

$=2(1+4+1)+(1-2+1)$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{a}=12$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift
